## Why This Is Asked
Tests knowledge of the Command pattern, runtime extensibility, and execution isolation in CLI tools. It also probes safe dynamic loading and simple governance for enabling/disabling commands.

## Key Concepts
- Command pattern and runtime registry
- Isolation per run and optional hooks
- Dynamic plugin-style extension without rebuilds

## Code Example
```javascript
// Minimal sketch
interface Command { name: string; description?: string; exec: (args: string[], ctx: any) => void | Promise<void> }
class Registry { register(n: string, c: Command){ /* store */ } resolve(n:string): Command|undefined{ } list(): string[] { } }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle name conflicts or versioned commands?
- How would you test commands with mocks for ctx?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates the ability to design runtime-extensible, tenant-aware policy composition without redeployments, and the capacity to justify pattern selection with correctness guarantees.

## Key Concepts

- **Runtime registry** for policy factories enables adding new policies without redeployment—new policies register themselves at startup or via dynamic configuration endpoints
- **Per-tenant isolation** achieved through separate pipeline instances and tenant-scoped context objects that flow through each policy stage
- **Execution order** controlled via ordered policy name arrays, allowing tenants to define their own pipeline sequences
- **Error handling** strategies include try-catch wrappers per policy, circuit breakers to prevent cascading failures, and graceful tenant-scoped fallback responses
- **Pattern trade-offs**: Chain of Responsibility provides simplicity and clarity but offers no built-in retry logic; for more complex scenarios, consider the Pipeline pattern with middleware or a dedicated workflow engine

## Why This Is Asked
This question probes designing a scalable, extensible command-dispatch system with runtime pluggability, ordering guarantees, and per-handler policies.

## Key Concepts
- Command Pattern and Mediator
- Runtime registries and type-safe dispatch
- Per-type queuing, concurrency, backpressure
- Policy hooks (retry, concurrency) and isolation

## Code Example
```javascript
interface Command { type: string; payload: any }
interface ICommandHandler { handle(cmd: Command): Promise<any> }
interface IPolicy { apply(context: any): void }
class Registry { register(type: string, h: ICommandHandler) { /* ... */ } lookup(type: string): ICommandHandler | undefined { /* ... */ } }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you detect and prevent circular registrations?
- How would you test order guarantees under load?
- What are trade-offs vs a pure Mediator vs Event-driven approach?
